findings.detail: The filing prints total investments of $1,153,413,327 as 185.82%, while balance-sheet net assets of $620,958,706 imply 185.7472%; the identity check assumes a denominator the filing's percentage column does not exactly use.

rationale: Class 3 anchor triangulation shows no extracted fair-value error: the SOI total and the independent fair-value hierarchy both report $1,153,413,327. The filing itself reports that amount as 185.82% of net assets, whereas the balance-sheet total net assets of $620,958,706 produce 185.7472%. Thus the aggregate 5.49% firing arises from applying the balance-sheet denominator to filer-reported percentages that use a slightly different filing-level denominator, not from a localized bad holding value. Treat the rule fire as an anchor/rule-scope false alarm.
